# Policy-KB bijection audit — energy_delivery_desk / task 0

Scope: product `energy` ("Refined Fuels and Propane Accounts"), 71 published documents under `env/env_0003_farm_supply_and_grain_cooperative/docs/energy/`, against `env/env_0003_farm_supply_and_grain_cooperative/tasks/energy_delivery_desk/energy.extended.yaml` and `task_tools.py`. The scan below is **whole-domain** and shared by both tasks of this difficulty; task 1's file records the same scan and its own dependency-form reading.

Entry conditions cited, not re-run: the difficulty's source-layer verdict is PASS at round 2 (task 0 PASS, task 1 PASS on all four relationships); `check_docs.py env/farm_supply_and_grain_cooperative energy` reported `docs=71 roles={'facet': 10, 'factor': 36, 'baseline': 7, 'hub': 7, 'policy': 11} … required quantitative keys=154 task_tools=7 prerequisite edges=5 … DOCS OK`; `check_traceability.py …/energy_delivery_desk` reported `task 0.json copied 20 missing 0 ok True`, `1.json copied 23 missing 0 ok True`, `TRACEABILITY OK`. The runtime-visible view and the DB access path were supplied and were used in tool form. No input was missing.

Ordering connective and strength: each sentence keeps the source's own connective ("only after" ×4, "Before … must carry" ×1) and its hard-gate strength; none is softened to advice, none is turned from a sufficient into a necessary condition or back. The depended-on policies' documents carry **no** prerequisite sentence of the blocked side — verified by the same search: each sentence has exactly one home.

Resolution basis, edge by edge (the sentence + the depended-on rules + the records):

1. **Clearance ← protection credit.** Sentence names the state "the account carries … a downside protection credit dated in the month the amount is worked out". `crediting_downside_protection_to_a_members_account_561fb402` states the depended-on rule — "the desk works the money out and records it against that booking … it is dated the day the desk works it out" — in the same words the state uses ("downside protection", "credit", "dated"), and `working_out_a_downside_protection_credit_777bb283` supplies the method. The records name the state in the same words: the ledger's `energy_price_protection_credited` rows dated 2026-06-30 and 2026-07-31. Resolvable at the source's strength.
2. **Clearance ← true-up.** Sentence names the state "the account must carry the true-up entry owed for every budget plan year that has passed its reconciliation date". `billing_the_budget_plan_true_up_e01f5931` states the write in those words — "puts the result onto the account as a single true-up line among the instalments billed there" — and `level_payment_plan_settings_by_programme_b8a56b3f` supplies the reconciliation date (15 July) that fixes which plan years have passed it. Records: eleven `energy_budget_installment_billed` rows and no true-up row. Resolvable.
3. **Price ← booking.** State: "the gallons standing to the member's credit take in every signed pre-buy request registered with the energy desk". `lodging_signed_pre_buy_gallons_to_a_members_credit_84f27b0a` — "those gallons are put to the member's own credit on the account as a single pre-buy booking line … From then on the booked gallons stand to the member's credit". Records: `contract_gallons: 0` / `current_gallons_owed: 0` against a registered signed request. Resolvable.
4. **Undrawn ← price.** State: "the account's contracted price of record stands at a price worked out from the bookings the account carries". `rewriting_the_contracted_price_carried_on_an_account_fb1d3081` + `arriving_at_the_contracted_price_of_record_91516f7c` (the weighted average **of the bookings**). Records: `contract_price_per_gallon: 0.0`. Resolvable.
5. **Closure ← undrawn.** State: "the account carries … the money applied against a booking when gallons standing undrawn were released". `settling_undrawn_gallons_against_a_booking_e5ece77e` — "the desk releases them and applies the money they come to against that booking" — plus `releasing_gallons_standing_undrawn_on_a_booking_7e45c1c0`. Records: `find_energy_orders` shows a registered signed request; the ledger shows no such entry. Resolvable.

`condition`, `resolved_by`, `effect`, `kind` and `gate` are authoring fields; searched for and found in **no** document.

> `energy_ext_protection_floor_credit.factors[undrawn_holdback_basis].ladder[0].method` says "less **the gauge reading the driver recorded at the most recent stop**". `energy_deliveries` carries two such readings per stop (`tank_percent_before`, `tank_percent_after`); the sentence names neither, and only the un-renderable `compute` binding `last_gauge_after: LATEST('energy_deliveries','tank_percent_after', …)` fixes the choice. `docs/energy/gallons_held_back_for_the_next_automatic_fill_8a29d5db.json` carries that sentence verbatim, so the **document is a faithful translation of the rule**; the rule is what does not entail a single number.

- `energy_ext_closure_settlement`'s baseline prose says "less the money applied against those bookings **when gallons standing undrawn were released**", while its `compute` takes `released_d = SUM(… event_type='energy_contract_gallons_drawn')`, which also sweeps ordinary contract fills. Task 1's account has no contract fills, so the two agree there. The KB carries the source's words verbatim.

The member's recollection of having signed does not stand in place of the record." Time anchors, boundaries (inclusive/exclusive), object correlation, acting base, order, cap and rounding are all carried as the source pins them; the retired `late_charge_after_grace` temporal basis is carried, correctly, in the past tense.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.**

Every normative atom of this difficulty's structured source is entailed by the published documents, with nothing unborne, nothing borne with changed meaning, and no claim from outside the source. All five prerequisite sentences stand verbatim, in the declared state form, in a document of the policy they block and in no other policy's. All ten retired clauses are borne and marked retired. All seven baselines are complete and all thirty-six factor ladders carry every tier with every threshold in figures.

Recorded alongside, and **not** counted against this verdict (Step 4 discipline — the faithful side is the policy, and a policy-side ambiguity is not re-judged as a document defect):
- **Policy-side note P1 (consequential).** `energy_ext_protection_floor_credit.factors[undrawn_holdback_basis].ladder[0].method` does not name which of the two driver-recorded gauge readings a stop's reading is; only `compute` does. This is what makes task 0's blind audit fail (see `runtime_context/.../0.md`). The semantics the visible materials fail to fix is: *which recorded gauge reading of a stop the tier means*. No remedy is proposed here.
- **Policy-side note P2 (latent).** `energy_ext_closure_settlement` baseline prose narrows the released-money term to undrawn releases while its `compute` sweeps all `energy_contract_gallons_drawn` rows.
- **Policy-side note P3 (latent).** "Stops the member called in" is bound to `delivery_type='will_call'` by `compute` alone.
- **Document-side observation D1.** `gallons_held_back_for_the_next_automatic_fill_8a29d5db`'s added worked illustration ("The driver's gauge reading at the most recent stop was 35 percent…") supplies a figure that reads as the arrival gauge, closing a boundary the source leaves open and closing it away from the scored reading. It adds no rule and changes no sentence, so it is not itself a bijection failure; it is recorded because it is the document-side contributor to the task-0 miss.
- **Document-side observation D2.** `pre_buy_booking_window_and_gallon_limits_9422d0cb` (facet) states the `unused_contract_gallons_treatment` column as live — "Gallons left unused at expiry are credited at the lower of the contracted and the posted price … and rolled into the following contract year on the Bulk Farm Fuel Delivery and Cardtrol Fleet Fueling Accounts" — while `energy_ext_undrawn_gallons_disposition` retires the operative clause of `energy_contract_gallons_program` that gave effect to it. Not RED: `unused_contract_gallons_treatment` remains a live `variants` parameter that facet documents legitimately render; the override's own scope is expressly the closing case ("Where an account is being closed there is no following contract year to roll gallons into"), which `releasing_gallons_standing_undrawn_on_a_booking_7e45c1c0` states in its opening sentence, so the two are reconciled by scope on the visible surface and task 1's blind audit reconciled them without difficulty.

No previous revision exists for this difficulty; this is revision 1.

## dependency_form

Scanned: the hop marks of the frozen blind answers for both tasks (all eight hops marked **state-derived**, none pre-solved) plus a full read and a scripted scan of all 71 documents.

**Findings: none. KB-EXPLICIT PASS.**

Checked item by item against the list this scan is defined by:

1. **State-form sentence restated as an action, or naming a performer, a tool, a policy or another document.** None found. All five prerequisite sentences are pure state statements and their documents do not restate them in any other form.
2. **A dependency or an order between problems stated where no prerequisite sentence states one, or stated in a second document.** None. Each of the five sentences has exactly one home (verified by exact-substring search over all 71 documents), and no other sentence in the corpus orders one problem against another.
3. **A dependency table, checklist, roadmap, complete route, or several problems strung into a procedure.** None. No document mentions more than one of the seven extended problems' subjects as a sequence. The hubs are single-problem documents; the computation documents are single-quantity; the factor documents are single-ladder and reference nothing.
4. **Cross-problem operational guidance, or another problem's tool named inside a blocked problem's documents.** None — see the scripted scan in `kb_to_source`. Each tool name occurs in exactly one document, its own hub, inside that hub's own invocation block, which is expressly not a finding of this scan.
5. **A wrong/right contrast, a named mistake, or an example or FAQ that walks across problems.** None. Every FAQ ("Contract questions", "Points of judgement", "Two questions the desk is asked") stays inside one policy's own subject; every worked example is labelled hypothetical, uses non-task figures, and exercises one document's own rule.
6. **A title or opening that mirrors a task's situation.** None. Titles name general subjects — "Counting Chargeable Months on Deeply Overdue Refined Fuels and Propane Balances", "Standing of a Signed Pre-Buy Request and the Share It Allows", "Base of the Closing Charge Where a Refined Fuels Account Carries Booking Money". The two `on_request` hubs name their defining request type — "A Member Paying a Refined Fuels and Propane Account Clear", "A Member Closing a Refined Fuels and Propane Account" — which is that policy's general subject and expressly not a mirror. No title or opening restates either caller's situation, and neither caller's circumstances (bank drafts stopped in the spring; machinery sold and the diesel account finished with) appear anywhere.
7. **A depended-on document reachable only through the dependent document's phrasing.** None. Each depended-on document is reachable through the words the records and the prerequisite sentence use for the state — "downside protection credit" (ledger `energy_price_protection_credited`), "true-up" / "plan year" / "reconciliation" (`energy_budget_installment_billed` + the catalogue's true-up date), "gallons standing to the member's credit" (`contract_gallons` / `current_gallons_owed`), "contracted price of record" (`contract_price_per_gallon`), "money applied against a booking" / "gallons standing undrawn". Both blind audits found every one of them without using the dependent document's wording.
8. **A factor document that names a tier-holder, describes the mistake to avoid, or writes a task's evidence rows in as fact.** None. Every factor document states its ladder as a rule and leaves the tier to be derived. No "most members", no "certain customers qualify", no naming of any real row.
9. **A computation document hinting at variation, or a factor document pointing at the computation document or another factor.** None. The seven computation documents state their defaults flatly — "The settlement allowance is nothing."; "None of the money applied against pre-buy bookings is recognised."; "Nothing is loaded onto the average for downside protection."; "The administration charge is 75.00 USD."; "The closing charge runs for one month."; "The lot rule leaves the gallons unrounded."; "Nothing already credited is set against the credit." — with no "unless otherwise provided", no "adjustments may apply", no exception list and no pointer. A scripted scan for that whole family of hedges over all 71 documents returned nothing. No factor document names, overrides or points at a computation document or at another factor; the corpus is a discrete topology.

**Closest approach in the corpus, recorded and judged not RED.** `paying_an_energy_account_clear_6dcdca30`, final section:

> "## The plan year behind the balance
> An account that has carried a level payment plan closes its plan years against what the member actually used, and what that settling leaves stands among the instalments on the account. Before the amount that clears the account is worked out, the account must carry the true-up entry owed for every budget plan year that has passed its reconciliation date."

The first sentence explains, in the state's own vocabulary, what a "true-up entry among the instalments" is — the referent the prerequisite sentence names. It names no tool, no policy, no document, no performer, and no order beyond the source's own sentence that follows it, and it does not say who must do the settling or when. It is therefore a same-source explanation of the state's terms rather than an action-form restatement, and it is not recorded as a finding. It is set down here because it is the single place in the corpus that comes closest to the line.

**KB-EXPLICIT PASS.**

### D1 — the illustration. Verified closed, and closed for the right reason.

This was the item flagged as most worth scrutiny, and it is the one that was actively pulling a reader away from the scored reading.

Round 1 text: *"The driver's gauge reading at the most recent stop was 35 percent. The held-back gallons are 80 percent less 35 percent of 1000.0 gallons, coming to 450.0 gallons."* — a figure that read as the arrival gauge, against a rule sentence that named neither reading and a binding that took the other.

Round 2 text (`gallons_held_back_for_the_next_automatic_fill_8a29d5db.json`, "Worked illustrations"):

> "*A busy automatic account.* A tank of 1000.0 gallons water capacity stands on the automatic keep-full schedule on a programme whose fill-to percentage is 80 percent, and 5 stops were made on the account in the twelve months ending on the handling date. **At the most recent stop the driver's gauge read 35 percent on arriving, before any fuel was pumped, and 80 percent once the fill was finished. The first line takes the arrival reading of 35 percent**, so the held-back gallons are 80 percent less 35 percent of 1000.0 gallons, coming to 450.0 gallons."

Judged against the three things that could still be wrong with it:

1. **Does it now agree with the rule, or still close something the rule leaves open?** It agrees. The rule sentence itself now says "the gauge reading the driver took on arriving at the most recent stop, **before any fuel was pumped**" — the boundary is closed in the *source*, and the illustration merely instantiates it. The illustration's hypothetical inputs supply both readings so the instantiation is checkable; supplying both is what makes it an illustration of the rule rather than a second rule.
2. **Is it a wrong/right contrast or a named mistake?** No. "The first line takes the arrival reading of 35 percent" states which reading the line takes. It does not name the other reading as an error, does not say "not the after reading", does not describe what a reader without the rule would do, and does not label anything a mistake. The distinction it draws is the source sentence's own distinction.
3. **Does it write a task's evidence in as fact?** No. 1000.0 gallons / 80 percent / 5 stops / 35 percent / 80 percent are not this account's figures (1000 gallons capacity is, but 6 stops, 44.0 and 74.0 are the real ones), the section is headed "Worked illustrations (hypothetical inputs)", and nothing names a tier this or any customer sits on.

The companion section added beside it — "## The reading the first line takes — The gauge reading the first line is measured from is the arrival reading of the most recent stop: what the driver's gauge showed on arriving at the site, before any fuel was pumped." — is a same-source restatement of the sentence in its own document. It replaces nothing, contrasts nothing and points nowhere. **D1 closed.**

### The three residual prose/binding divergences, and the coordinator's reasoning

The source-layer auditor recorded three sentences of the same shape as round 1's finding. Verified each on the published corpus and the records rather than accepting the "inert" claim:

| # | Divergence | Verified on both worlds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a | prose "posted on the account" / "the day of the most recent payment" against bindings that read `delivery_date`, where each ledger row carries both `delivery_date` and `posted_date` | `find_energy_deliveries` on both accounts: **`delivery_date == posted_date` on all 38 rows of task 0 and all 18 rows of task 1**. Genuinely inert. |
| b | prose "stood registered" / "lodged with the energy desk" against `requested_date`, where the request row carries both `requested_date` and `received_at` | `find_energy_orders`: `requested_date` 2025-11-20, `received_at` 2025-11-20 09:12:00 CST — the same calendar day, so 11 whole months on either reading. Inert. |
| c | "the bookings standing on the account" bound to all bookings | Task 1 carries exactly one booking with nothing drawn against it, so the two sets coincide; task 0 does not score the contract-price policy. Inert. |

**The coordinator's reasoning is right for this round, with one qualification worth carrying forward.** Right, because this skill's verdicts are the three it defines: a reading that cannot separate on either world cannot make a blind derivation diverge (no KB-RUNTIME RED), and in all three cases the KB carries the source sentence verbatim, so there is nothing for the two-way scan to catch either (no KB-BIJECTION RED). Neither is a defect of the documents.

The qualification: their inertness is a property of the **seeds**, not of the rules. Round 1's RED was the same shape and was caught only because the seeds happened to separate the two readings by 300 gallons. Reseed either world — a payment posted a day after the delivery it answers, a request received the day after it is dated, a second partly-drawn booking on an account whose contracted price is scored — and the same failure mode returns, with no gate to catch it, because `check_docs.py` proves verbatim carriage (which would still hold) and `check_traceability.py` proves copyability (which would still hold). So the right disposition is not "closed" but "standing policy-side note, inert under the present seeds", and a reseed of this difficulty should re-test them before trusting them. I would not route them to a source round now either.
